clauses.text:
1-101. The obligations of the Agreement on Government Procurement (Agree­
ment on Government Procurement, General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade,  
12 April 1979, Geneva (GATT 1979)) apply to any procurement of eligible  
products by the Executive agencies listed in the Annex to this Order (eligible  
products are defined in Section 308 of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979; 19  
U.S.C. 2518(4)). Such procurement shall be in accord with the policies and  
procedures of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (41 U.S.C. 401 e t  s e q .) .

1-102. The United States Trade Representative, hereinafter referred to as the  
Trade Representative, shall be responsible for interpretation of the Agree­
ment. The Trade Representative shall seek the advice of the interagency  
organization established under Section 242(a) of the Trade Expansion Act of  
1962 (19 U.S.C. 1872(a)) and consult with affected Executive agencies, includ­
ing the Office of Federal Procurement Policy.

1-103. The ^interpretation of Article VIII:1 of the Agreement shall be subject to  
the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense.

1-104. The Trade Representative shall determine, from time to time, the dollar  
equivalent of 150,000 Special Drawing Right units and shall publish that 
determination in the Federal Register. Procurement of less than 150,000 Special  
Drawing Right units is not subject to the Agreement or this Order (Article  
I:l(b) of the Agreement).

1-105. In order to ensure coordination of international trade policy with regard  
to the implementation of the Agreement, agencies shall consult in advance  
with the Trade Representative about negotiations with foreign governments or  
instrumentalities which concern government procurement.
1-2. D e l e g a t i o n s  a n d  A u t h o r i z a t i o n .

1-201. The functions vested in the President by Sections 301, 302, 304, 305(c)  
and 306 of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979 (19 U.S.C. 2511, 2512, 2514,  
2515(c) and 2516) are delegated to the Trade Representative.

1-202. Notwithstanding the delegation in Section 1-201, the Secretary of  
Defense is authorized, in accord with Section 302(b)(3) of the Trade Agree­
ments Act of 1979 (19 U.S.C. 2512(b)(3)), to waive the prohibitions specified
therein.

Executive Order 12260 of December 31, 1980
Agreement on Government Procurement
By the authority vested in me as President by the Constitution and statutes of  
the United States of America, including Title III of the Trade Agreements Act  
of 1979 (19 U.S.C. 2511-2518), and Section 301 of Title 3 of the United States  
Code, and in order to implement the Agreement on Government Procurement,  
as defined in 19 U.S.C. 2518(1), it is hereby ordered as follows:
1-1 R e s p o n s i b i l i t i e s .
1-101. The obligations of the Agreement on Government Procurement (Agree­
ment on Government Procurement, General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade,  
12 April 1979, Geneva (GATT 1979)) apply to any procurement of eligible  
products by the Executive agencies listed in the Annex to this Order (eligible  
products are defined in Section 308 of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979; 19  
U.S.C. 2518(4)). Such procurement shall be in accord with the policies and  
procedures of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy (41 U.S.C. 401 e t  s e q .) .
1-102. The United States Trade Representative, hereinafter referred to as the  
Trade Representative, shall be responsible for interpretation of the Agree­
ment. The Trade Representative shall seek the advice of the interagency  
organization established under Section 242(a) of the Trade Expansion Act of  
1962 (19 U.S.C. 1872(a)) and consult with affected Executive agencies, includ­
ing the Office of Federal Procurement Policy.
1-103. The ^interpretation of Article VIII:1 of the Agreement shall be subject to  
the concurrence of the Secretary of Defense.
1-104. The Trade Representative shall determine, from time to time, the dollar  
equivalent of 150,000 Special Drawing Right units and shall publish that 
determination in the Federal Register. Procurement of less than 150,000 Special  
Drawing Right units is not subject to the Agreement or this Order (Article  
I:l(b) of the Agreement).
1-105. In order to ensure coordination of international trade policy with regard  
to the implementation of the Agreement, agencies shall consult in advance  
with the Trade Representative about negotiations with foreign governments or  
instrumentalities which concern government procurement.
1-2. D e l e g a t i o n s  a n d  A u t h o r i z a t i o n .
1-201. The functions vested in the President by Sections 301, 302, 304, 305(c)  
and 306 of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979 (19 U.S.C. 2511, 2512, 2514,  
2515(c) and 2516) are delegated to the Trade Representative.
1-202. Notwithstanding the delegation in Section 1-201, the Secretary of  
Defense is authorized, in accord with Section 302(b)(3) of the Trade Agree­
ments Act of 1979 (19 U.S.C. 2512(b)(3)), to waive the prohibitions specified
therein.
THE WHITE HOUSE,

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: Executive Order 12260 of December 31, 1980, 46 FR 1653, held at jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_12260.txt; it implements the Agreement on Government Procurement under Title III of the Trade Agreements Act of 1979 (obligations apply to listed agencies in the Annex; Trade Representative interprets and sets the dollar equivalent; sec. 1-201 delegates the President's functions under 19 U.S.C. 2511, 2512, 2514, 2515(c) and 2516; sec. 1-202 Secretary of Defense waiver). Later instruments, all amendments: EO 12347 (Feb. 23, 1982) adds the Maritime Administration to the Annex; EO 12388 (Oct. 14, 1982; effective Aug. 24, 1982 under its sec. 6) renames an agency in the Annex; EO 12474 (Apr. 17, 1984) removes, renames and adds Annex items and cites 19 U.S.C. 2511 et seq.; EO 13118 sec. 10(7) (Mar. 31, 1999; effective Apr. 1, 1999 under its sec. 11) replaces an agency name in the Annex; EO 13284 sec. 12 (Jan. 23, 2003; effective Jan. 24, 2003 under its sec. 21) adds the Department of Homeland Security to the Annex. OFR catalog notes record each as an amendment; none says Revoked or Superseded. Searches of held texts for the number also find Federal Register notices from 1994 through 2026 citing the order; the 2016 and 2026 USTR notices apply it, and the 2026 notice says the thresholds are determined in conformity with the order. Bounded searches read for coverage: current-law:usc (U.S. Code release point 119-121 USLM text and notes, citations of the order by number, edition current through 2026-10-09, laws enacted 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14 not reflected), current-law:ecfr (eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 plus GovInfo CFR bulk XML, 49 titles) and later-events:ofr_catalog (Office of the Federal Register disposition notes of 6941 catalog records plus operative sentences in 17521 saved order texts). 
Member checks: {"earlier_end_check":"Own text has no duration or condition. The five later orders only amend the Annex or preamble; no held order or statute revokes or supersedes the order, and the USTR notice of February 2026 applies it.","independent_command_check":"Independent commands: none outside the order; the Trade Representative's threshold notices are acts under sec. 1-104, not separate instruments ending or extending it.","savings_check":"No savings question arises: the order remains operative, no ending, repeal or revocation is claimed, and no residual effect separate from the continuing clauses is claimed. The bounded searches found no ending that would leave residual effects.","scope_check":"One clause covering the whole order; the Annex amendments change which agencies are listed and the clause continues amended."}

reviews.reasons: Identity (EO 12260, Dec. 31, 1980, 46 FR 1653, Carter) and quotes check; the single clause covers the operative sections 1-101 to 1-202, with the Annex referenced. The OFR note lists five amending orders, all held, and their effective dates in later_events are correct. The current Code note to 19 U.S.C. 2511 prints the order as amended with no ending statement, the 19 U.S.C. 2512/2514/2515 notes cite sec. 1-201, and the USTR notice of Feb. 3, 2026 applies the order, so the operative YES is well supported. But the judgment_reason says the five orders amended the preamble and Annex; each amends the Annex only. The preamble is unchanged in the current Code note. Every stated fact must match the sources, so the claim is rejected for this misstatement; changing the wording to the Annex only would cure it.
